fit_poly_surface — 3D surface_fit op

• Data kinds: image2d × image2d × image2d → poly_surface

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.fit_poly_surface(x, y, z, degree=2) (to call the implementation directly, import match3d; match3d.fit_poly_surface(x, y, z, degree=2); from the registry, ops3d.get("fit_poly_surface"))

Usage

Scattered (x,y,z) → a polynomial least-squares z=f(x,y). Returns model (coef/powers/degree/rms/pv).

Fits the basis {x^i·y^j : i + j <= degree} (number of terms (degree+1)(degree+2)/2; degree=1 gives a 3-term plane, 2 a 6-term 2nd-order surface) with lstsq. x, y, z may have any shape as long as they have the same number of elements (raveled internally; for a grid, pass the output of np.mgrid as is). Return dict: coef (T,) coefficients, powers the (i, j) of each coefficient (term x**i * y**j), degree, rms the residual RMS, pv the residual peak-to-valley (max − min). Units are those of z.

• With fewer points than terms, the minimum-norm solution is returned silently. Large magnitudes of x, y make high orders ill-conditioned

(centre and normalise the coordinates first). No NaN check.

Downstream: evaluate at arbitrary points with eval_poly_surface(model, x, y). For a height field on a grid, surface_form_error / background_flatten call this internally.
